trigger: an exports line whose only client is a world-equivalent spec: 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0, ?*, or BSD -network 0.0.0.0 -mask 0.0.0.0
classification_rationale: README and YAML field_5 promise anonymous means guest or world access; the code only treats an empty client or a literal * as anonymous.
summary: Cluster G-A, reported by the security-guardian (SG-1), happy-path (HP-1) and cross-platform (XP-2) reviewers independently; the unhappy-path reviewer (UP-1) echoed it. Probe output: share|nfs|-|/srv|rw|false|clients_1|exports. Native label was MEDIUM; derived I3 with no exposure modifier is HIGH and governs. Two reviewers noted it would fall to I7/MEDIUM only if the field were redefined as the literal * spec.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted, widen the code not the wording. detail::is_world_client / is_zero_addr now serve parse_spec and the BSD -network/-mask handling; client stays counted; tests per spelling plus 10.0.0.0/8, bare 0.0.0.0 and non-zero-mask negatives; README and YAML field_5 reworded and docs regenerated. The BSD half of the change travelled with the macOS leg that was later split out (b81d8c68d); the delta wave re-reviewed the Linux half (see g1/g2 H1).

trigger: (a) a macOS exports line with -maproot=root|0 or -mapall=root; (b) a Linux option list such as no_root_squash,root_squash or no_root_squash,all_squash
classification_rationale: The no_root_squash flag is absent where root is not squashed (BSD) and present where a later option re-squashes root (Linux), so the flag misreports the posture.
summary: Cluster G-B, reported by the happy-path (HP-2) and cross-platform (XP-3) reviewers independently. (a) parse_bsd_exports dropped every -option except ro/o/offline/network/mask; (b) apply_opt only ever set no_root_squash. Probe verified on the plugin side; the nfs-utils last-wins semantics were reasoned from memory by the reviewer and checked by the Architect against the kernel nfsd_setuser source and the exports man text. Native label MEDIUM; derived I3 is HIGH and governs.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. ExportDefaults carries root_squash/all_squash with in-order set and clear; a segment contributes the flag only when neither applies; BSD -maproot=/-mapall= naming root or 0 raises it; the initial nrs seed was dropped so a line-default -no_root_squash overridden by a spec's own root_squash is not flagged. Seven test rows. The BSD half later left this PR with the macOS leg (b81d8c68d).

trigger: smb.conf share with read only = yes plus a non-empty write list, or read only = no plus a read list
classification_rationale: README defines mixed generally, but SMB access is derived from read only alone, so a share a write-list member can write reports ro and mixed is never emitted for SMB.
summary: Cluster G-C, reported by the happy-path (HP-3) and security-guardian (SG-3) reviewers independently. Plugin behaviour verified by probe; the Samba side is from smb.conf(5), smbd was not run. Native label MEDIUM; derived I3 is HIGH and governs.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted - the reviewer's rule (either list non-empty means mixed) overstated smb.conf(5), so access is mixed only when a list contradicts the default (ro plus non-empty write list, or rw plus non-empty read list). writelist/readlist resolve through the existing lookup chain; values are never emitted; four combinations, the empty list and copy/[global] inheritance are tested.

trigger: (i) agent cannot search a parent of the default usershares dir (EACCES/EIO on lstat); (ii) smb.conf usershare path inside a dead hard NFS/CIFS mount; (iii) stock Debian samba with the key unset
classification_rationale: dir_exists returns a bool so a refused or failed lstat reads as absent, breaking the refused-never-reads-as-absent invariant while status stays supported.
summary: Cluster G-D: security-guardian SG-2 (native LOW, derived I3 HIGH by table, narrow trigger), sre SRE-1 and unhappy-path UP-14 (I5 MEDIUM, lstat of a config-supplied path with no deadline), enterprise-readiness ER-1 (I8, permanent constrained on stock Debian samba); the happy-path reviewer noted the same stock-host noise. Four reporters. The derived HIGH from I3 governs the gate; native labels were lower.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. SmbConf.usershares_off added and the config-supplied usershare path lstat removed; list_linux skips the probe when usershares are configured or explicitly off and otherwise probes the DEFAULT dir only; LinuxFs::dir_probe is tri-state and any errno other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR yields linux:shares:smb_conf:usershares_unreadable (constrained). ER-1 was ruled not noise: a stock Debian host with the directory present does run usershares the plugin cannot list, so constrained plus usershares_not_read is the truth. README token row and caveat added; legs and posix_fs tests added (EACCES case skipped as root). The explicit-zero versus set-path precedence was refined later (see cr2 SPEC-5, 7322875dc).

trigger: smb.conf with include, config backend = registry or guest ok placed before the first [header], or a global config file redirect
classification_rationale: parse_ini drops every key before the first header, but Samba treats a headerless preamble as [global], so the plugin reports supported while missing include/registry and global defaults.
summary: Cluster G-E item UP-2, one reporter (unhappy-path). Plugin behaviour verified; that Samba treats a headerless preamble as [global] and honours config file was reasoned, not run. Reviewer noted practical impact LOW-MEDIUM; derived I3 is HIGH by table and gates.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. parse_smb_conf prepends [global] to the folded text so preamble keys, include, config backend and guest ok land where Samba puts them (shared ini_parse.hpp untouched); a global config file counts as include_present; README row widened; preamble tests at parser and legs level.

trigger: UTF-8 BOM before the first line of smb.conf or exports, or an unterminated [header, a relative or option-first exports line
classification_rationale: A line the parser cannot read is skipped with no count and the result stays supported.
summary: Cluster G-E item UP-3, one reporter (unhappy-path). BOM first-line drop verified for both parsers; the reviewer itself noted nfsd also rejects BOM-prefixed exports lines and Samba BOM tolerance is unverified. Reviewer practical band LOW-MEDIUM; derived I3 is HIGH by table.

Rejected as a code defect in the governance r1 round (documented in 8a8e4441a): no BOM stripping and no skipped-line counter. Architect ruling: adapted to docs only. Stripping the BOM from exports would REPORT a share nfsd does not export (nfs-utils rejects a line whose first token does not start with /), the wrong direction; Samba tolerance of a BOM or an unterminated header is unverified and a malformed smb.conf fails the whole load, which no per-line counter would model. README caveat 2 gained one sentence stating that such lines are skipped without a count, as nfsd and testparm reject them too.
adjudicated_by: the Architect adjudicator of the snr-dev run (independent of the proposing reviewer and of the author)
adjudication_rationale: The finding is derived HIGH (I3, no exposure modifier) and the terminal disposition rejects the code change, so this row weakens the gate and carries an adjudicator. Basis: the exports half is behaviour-matching (nfsd skips the same lines), the smb.conf half is unverified and unmodelled by any counter, and the reviewer's own practical band was LOW-MEDIUM. Independence is asserted, not verified: the adjudicator is a subagent of the authoring session and the field is free text.

trigger: exports line /k "unterminated, "foo" *(rw), -network with no value, or an smb.conf header []
classification_rationale: A quoted token bypassed the absolute-path check in both exports parsers, so invalid lines produced phantom shares, and an empty section name produced a share named -.
summary: Cluster G-E item UP-4, one reporter (unhappy-path), verified by probe in both parsers. Reviewer practical band LOW (an admin-typed invalid line); derived I3 is HIGH by table.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Quoted-path exemption removed, BSD path list stops at a non-absolute token, -network counts only with a value, empty section name skipped; one test row each.

trigger: any Mac with no share points (sharing -l -f json prints plain text instead of JSON)
classification_rationale: The empty-list text 'No share point records.' is neither blank nor JSON, so a zero-share host reads unrecognised_output / constrained and can never report supported.
summary: Reported by cross-platform (XP-1). Verified in the binary's disassembly and by running the parser on the literal (recognised=0); a live zero-share run was not possible and the exit code on that path is unconfirmed. Native SHOULD agrees with derived I6 MEDIUM.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. kNoSharePoints recognised by parse_sharing_json and exempted from the exit_nonzero arm in list_macos, so the fix needs only spawn success; exit 0 and 1 tested; the invented {} case relabelled synthetic; README caveat says the text comes from the binary's string table.

The macOS leg (list_macos, parse_sharing_json, kNoSharePoints and the sharing spawn) left this change as its own review unit in b81d8c68d (ship the Linux leg first, leave macOS planned). The 8a8e4441a fix travels with that follow-up PR; this PR now ships a macOS placeholder only.

trigger: RBAC on; an administrator dispatches shares.list; a Viewer queries /api/responses/<id>
classification_rationale: 'Gated at Infrastructure:Read' is true for dispatch only; stored output is read via Response:Read, which a Viewer holds.
summary: Reported by compliance-officer (CO-1), CC6.1. The generic Response gate is pre-existing and identical for every plugin; only the sentence is introduced, so provenance is recorded introduced. Native MEDIUM agrees with derived I7 MEDIUM.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Reworded at the README sensitivity bullet, README caveat 5 and the changelog fragment to say dispatch is gated at Infrastructure:Read and the stored result is readable by Response:Read holders, as for every plugin. The Response gate was not touched.

trigger: a refactor flips the unset read only default to rw
classification_rationale: No test asserts access for a share that sets neither read only nor writable, so a wrong-result regression is invisible.
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-1) from ~50 verified mutants (P1 and M24 survive). I3 if regressed, I9 today; the reviewer's SHOULD band is kept as the stronger label (label governs when stronger than the recorded facts).
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Default read-only = yes case added (share with no read only key, and [global] with none).

trigger: section header [a\xC0\xAF|b] or a sharing smb_name with overlong, surrogate or NUL bytes
classification_rationale: The wire-safety claim is proven only on the NFS path field; the scrub-removal mutant H1 survives for SMB names.
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-2). I1 if regressed (invalid UTF-8 on the wire), I9 today; reviewer band SHOULD kept as the stronger label.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted; fixer adapted the sharing leg: nlohmann rejects raw ill-formed UTF-8 in JSON so overlong/surrogate cannot reach that path and are covered via the smb section name; separate hostile-name cases added (smb section with overlong bytes and a pipe; sharing smb_name with NUL, pipe, backslash, CRLF).

trigger: exports.d with more than 4096 entries or a readdir error
classification_rationale: The 4096-entry cap and the readdir-error arm have no test; the literals 256 KiB, 64 and 4096 are used symbolically so mutants survive (G4, G5, G7, G11).
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-3). I5/I8 if regressed (unbounded listing); reviewer band SHOULD for G4/G5, LOW for the symbolic constants.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. Paths.max_dir_entries injected (default kMaxDirEntries) so a cap of 5 over 7 snippets gives too_many with no 4097-file test; static_asserts pin 256 KiB, 64 and 4096. The readdir-error arm stays untestable portably and a test comment says so.

trigger: a reader or reviewer weighs the populated Linux fixtures against the standing fixtures-from-real-captures rule
classification_rationale: Populated exports / exports.d / smb.conf inputs are labelled RECONSTRUCTION although a real seeded-container capture produced docs/samples/linux.txt and its inputs were not wired into a test.
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-4). Labels were honest; the gap is the tie between the captured inputs and the sample rows.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. The seeded inputs were preserved in the capture script heredocs and are committed verbatim as SEEDED INPUT fixtures in test_shares_parsers.cpp with a case asserting the sample's five share rows byte for byte; README fixture note updated. No probe sources or unwired capture files were committed.

trigger: an operator or automation keys on source|exports_d|failed for too_many, using the README
classification_rationale: The Result status table says the exports_d source row says failed for every cause, but too_many keeps the source row at read and EACCES/EPERM is refused.
summary: Reported by docs-writer (DW-1). Guidance fails visibly (the token still appears and the data is partial but correct), so I8 LOW rather than I4.
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. too_many split into its own README row (source stays read, excess entries cut) and EACCES/EPERM stated as refused.

trigger: a reader takes 'never follows a symlink' to cover ancestor directories such as macOS /etc
classification_rationale: The shared primitive applies O_NOFOLLOW to the final path component only; ancestors are followed. The narrower statements elsewhere in the README are correct.
summary: Reported by docs-writer (DW-2); the security-guardian confirmed the truth call. Not I6(a): the control is advertised accurately elsewhere.
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Both README sentences now say final path component only, with ancestors such as macOS /etc followed.

trigger: a maintainer reads the comment on for_each_logical_line
classification_rationale: The comment says a physical line beginning with # or ; never continues; the code tests this only for the first physical line of a logical line.
summary: Reported by docs-writer (DW-3); truth owner is the C++ reviewer.
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Comment reworded to 'the first physical line of a logical line'.

trigger: a maintainer reads the comment at test_shares_local_dispatcher.cpp:227
classification_rationale: The comment excepts a tool that could not start from the 'two source rows on every arm' claim while the code always emits both rows.
summary: Reported by docs-writer (DW-4).
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Comment reworded: both source rows appear on every arm, including a sharing that could not start.

trigger: a maintainer reads the comment at shares_posix_fs.hpp:76; or a genuine ancestor symlink loop under exports.d
classification_rationale: The comment says macOS answers ELOOP for a symlinked directory under O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW; two independent probes show ENOTDIR on both platforms, so the ELOOP map is dead and would mislabel a real loop as not_a_directory.
summary: Reported independently by cross-platform (XP-4) and quality-engineer (QE-5); both ran the open on macOS 26.6. Wrong outcome is benign (an unmapped ELOOP would still be failed, never absent).
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. ELOOP-to-ENOTDIR map removed (an ELOOP now surfaces as failed/eloop) and the comment says both platforms answer ENOTDIR.

trigger: none fires; a future refactor of the retained directory handle
classification_rationale: The relist (closes the previous DIR*) and read-without-open (EBADF) cleanup paths that the resource ledger relies on had no test.
summary: Reported by cpp-safety (F1). The reviewer's brief labelled it SHOULD but derived INFO (I9, E6: wrong outcome proven unable to occur, with a retained-fd probe) and stated that the derived band governs; severity_native records the reviewer's SHOULD and severity_mapped the derived NICE.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. 200 relists with a constant open-fd count (fcntl scan), relist onto a plain file gives ENOTDIR with the stale handle closed, read gives io/EBADF, and read before any listing also gives EBADF.

trigger: a future caller that copies LinuxFs or shares one across threads
classification_rationale: The header says exports.d is opened once, but the code reopens on every list_exports_d; nothing states that a LinuxFs is single-owner.
summary: Reported by cpp-safety (F2); today run_linux builds a fresh LinuxFs per execute so no shared state exists.
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Header now says opened per listing, one LinuxFs per execute(), not thread-safe, not for sharing.

trigger: a maintainer reads the test header
classification_rationale: The header still enumerates seams A-C and the three entry points; the shares execute_list seam D is not named and the SEAM C sentence now describes two seams.
summary: Reported by cpp-safety (F3).
Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. Header names seam D (yuzu::shares::execute_list) and the SEAMS C and D sentence is corrected.

trigger: maintenance (rename of ini_detail::trim), a future stdlib trimming transitive includes, bad_alloc while the plugin loads
classification_rationale: Three hygiene items: shares reaches into another header's private ini_detail::trim (cpp-expert CPP-1 and consistency-auditor N2); the new shared leaf ini_parse.hpp lacks <cstddef>/<utility> (CPP-2); a namespace-scope const Paths kPaths allocates at dlopen outside the ABI containment (CPP-3).
summary: Grouped fold of cpp-expert CPP-1/CPP-2/CPP-3 plus consistency-auditor N2. CPP-2 was labelled pre-existing (moved body) by the reviewer; recorded introduced because the shared header is new in this change (default when contested). CPP-3 is I5 in theory but not triggerable on a real host, so I9.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted/adapted. ini_detail::trim made public as yuzu::shared::ini_trim with the shares call sites following (mgmt_posture untouched, it never used it); ini_parse.hpp includes <cstddef>/<utility> and uses std::size_t; Paths is now built inside run_linux, net zero lines.

trigger: one section with a ~120 KB copy value plus ~500 sections copying it, in a root-writable smb.conf
classification_rationale: The copy target is lower-cased on every walk step; hostile input costs 0.46 s CPU at -O2 for one 256 KiB file.
summary: Reported by sre (SRE-2), measured. All other hostile shapes were fast.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. A copy target over 255 bytes sets copy_unresolved and stops the walk; a 300-byte parser test added. The bare 255 became a named constant in the code-review r2 round (7322875dc).

trigger: an operator wants to disable a default-on plugin; a reader trusts the 1 MiB wire claim; a reader trusts the registry description
classification_rationale: Three documentation gaps: the README never says the plugin is on by default or how to disable it (sre SRE-3, enterprise-readiness); the 1 MiB budget claim ignores pipe-escape doubling so the wire can reach about 2.1 MB (unhappy-path UP-9); the agent_registry.cpp description omits /etc/exports.d (consistency-auditor N4b).
summary: Grouped fold. sre cited I7 for SRE-3 but derived LOW because the plugin-readme standard has no mandated disable section; recorded I8 so the facts match the derived LOW. The generic per-plugin kill switch exists, so the omission is documentation only.

Fixed in 8a8e4441a (governance r1 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted. README bullet states default on, the generic kill switch endpoint and --plugin-allowlist; README row and caveat state the budget counts text before pipe-escaping and the wire can reach about twice that; /etc/exports.d added to the shares.list description (no test pins that string).

trigger: a future errno-token or status-contract change must be applied to every copy
classification_rationale: status_token / report_list / Listing / refused / errno_token are near-verbatim copies of the mgmt_posture helpers with a third variant in update_source_trust; no shared owner exists.
summary: Reported by consistency-auditor (N1) and noted by the architect; raised again in the code-review r2 Standards review (item 4). Architect ruling: correct observation, wrong PR - a shared status-row helper has no reverse dependency on shares and is its own primitive PR per the known-good split boundaries. Copies at mgmt_posture_legs.hpp:42-182, shares_legs.hpp:51-178 and update_source_trust. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: a refactor of copy depth, the relative usershare path fallback, or the 4096 name cut
classification_rationale: Surviving mutants: a 9-deep non-cyclic copy chain, the relative usershare path fallback, and the 4096 cut on SMB/JSON names are untested.
summary: Reported by quality-engineer (QE-6). Architect ruling: rejected as accepted coverage residue - the relative-path fallback was deleted by G-D, the depth-9 chain is covered by the cycle guard, and the 4096 cut shares detail::cut with the NFS-path test; listed in the PR body. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: an exports.d snippet unlinked between readdir and openat
classification_rationale: The vanished snippet is skipped silently; status stays supported and the exports_d count is short with no token.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-5). Architect ruling: rejected - a snapshot of a changing directory, deliberately continued with a comment; reporting it would make an unrelated admin edit a constrained listing. Listed in the PR body. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: a socket named *.exports in exports.d on macOS (errno_102); an exports.d snippet failure beside readable siblings
classification_rationale: A socket yields a bare errno_<n> token, and source|exports_d|failed|- drops the count although sibling snippets' rows were emitted.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-7). Architect ruling: rejected - errno_<n> is the documented fallback and the count rule is 'count only when read'; both are stated contracts. Listed in the PR body. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: smbd started with -s <other file>; the same path exported over NFS and SMB
classification_rationale: A command-line smb.conf override is invisible to any file read, and one path exported over two protocols appears as two rows.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-8). Architect ruling: rejected - an smbd -s override is invisible to any file read (README caveat 2 says configured, not live) and two rows for two protocols is the correct inventory. Listed in the PR body. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: sharing exits 0 with empty stdout; max_lines=8192 without stop_after_max_lines
classification_rationale: Exit 0 with empty or whitespace stdout reads as a recognised empty list, and the max_lines runner option is inert.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-12), speculative by the reviewer's own word for the first half. Architect ruling: rejected - the real zero-share output is now pinned (M-1) and max_lines matches the declared sink-manifest row and the mgmt_posture runner options. The macOS code left this PR with the leg split (b81d8c68d). Listed in the PR body. DEFERRED follow-up, issue not yet filed (needs operator go).

trigger: exports client 10.1.2.3/0, 1.2.3.4/0.0.0.0 or ::1/0 (non-zero base address with a zero prefix or all-zero mask)
classification_rationale: is_world_client required an all-zero ADDRESS, so a non-zero base with a zero mask (which matches every client) reads anonymous=false.
summary: Cluster H1: security-guardian SG-D1, unhappy-path UP-2 and a quality-engineer out-of-focus note, three independent. Parser outcome verified; nfs-utils mask semantics were reasoned by the reviewers from exports(5). Native SHOULD/MEDIUM; derived I3 HIGH governs. The unhappy-path reviewer labelled it pre-existing relative to the delta; recorded introduced because the whole plugin is new in this PR.

Fixed in 83ec0dba4 (governance r2 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adapted. Verified against nfs-utils 2.8.3 and 3.1.1 support/export/client.c: a dotted all-zero mask matches every client, so the dotted form is confirmed; the /0 prefix form is not reliably world in nfs-utils (shift by 32 is undefined) but is kept as the conservative direction. is_zero_v4/is_zero_v6 became is_v4(addr, zero_only)/is_v6(addr); world means a syntactically valid v4 or v6 literal with an all-zero v4 mask; ::::/0, 0.../0, :/0, host/0 stay rejected. Tests for 10.1.2.3/0, 1.2.3.4/0.0.0.0, ::1/0; field_5 wording and generated docs updated.

trigger: exports line "/srv/a 10.0.0.5(rw) 192.168.1.7(ro) with an unterminated double quote
classification_rationale: next_token runs an unterminated quote to end of line, so the rest of the line becomes the path: client addresses reach the wire contradicting the README, and a host-restricted line reads anonymous=true; nfsd would not export that path at all.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-1), verified by probe. Reviewer labelled it pre-existing relative to the delta; recorded introduced because the lexer is new in this PR. Native MEDIUM; derived I3 HIGH governs.

Fixed in 83ec0dba4 (governance r2 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted, confirmed against nfs-utils xgettok (an open quote runs past the newline, so nfsd never exports such a line). Tok gained an unterminated flag; parse_exports skips the line for an unterminated path token and for any later unterminated token; fixture line yields zero shares with a following sane line still parsed.

trigger: smb.conf [b] with copy = a followed by copy = c
classification_rationale: The merged map keeps the last copy line, so b gets the c values and copy_unresolved stays 0; the reviewer recalled Samba not overriding an already-copied parameter, which would give the a values.
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-3); the Samba side was from memory and explicitly not verified. Native LOW; derived I3 HIGH by table.

Rejected in the governance r2 round: the HIGH premise (wrong values) is refuted by Samba source. In lib/param/loadparm.c copy_service(dest, src, copymap) copies every P_LOCAL parameter whose copymap bit is set and does not modify the destination's copymap, and lpcfg_do_service_parameter clears a bit only for a key set locally, so a later copy line overwrites copied keys: the last copy line wins for every non-local key and local keys always win, exactly what the merged map plus lookup computes. The copy re-review's sequential Samba model (multiple copy lines included, 60k cases, 0 violations) agrees. What remains of the cluster is the two classification gaps recorded under g2-H3-LOW1-LOW2.
adjudicated_by: the Architect adjudicator of the snr-dev run (independent of the proposing reviewer and of the author)
adjudication_rationale: Derived HIGH finding rejected on source evidence read by the adjudicator (Samba lib/param/loadparm.c) rather than from memory; this weakens the gate on a live HIGH so it carries an adjudicator and travels to the operator as a for-operator ruling. Independence is asserted, not verified: the adjudicator is a subagent of the authoring session and the field is free text.

trigger: (1) [b] [a] copy = C then copy = b with C undefined; (2) [a] copy = global with no [global] header following
classification_rationale: Only the last copy line survives in the INI map so an earlier invalid copy line goes unseen (Samba fails the whole load), and copy = global is unflagged unless a [global] header follows (Samba: source not found).
summary: Reported by the copy pre-pass re-review (LOW-1 and LOW-2); it found no counterexample to the stated contract (fuzz, 0 violations) and neither item blocks. Values are unaffected for LOW-2; only the error classification differs.

Fixed in 83ec0dba4 (governance r2 gate-fix). Architect ruling: adopted, verified against Samba handle_copy / lpcfg_getservicebyname. fold_section_headers now records every copy line as (section, value) mirroring parse_ini's comment and header rules; the pre-pass iterates that vector and also flags a target of global. SmbConf::copy_unresolved comment, parse_smb_conf comment and README row updated; tests for both shapes.

trigger: a counter refactor in the IPv6 zero-address helper

Rejected by cross-examination and by the Architect, by code. (b) shares_parsers.hpp:393-396: an unquoted token starting with - goes to the line-default branch and is never pushed to specs, so a bare - is not counted. (c) neither exports(5) nor xgettok has a ; comment character (comments are # only), so ;junk is a host token in nfs-utils too and whether it resolves is live state, out of scope.

Recorded as rejected, matching the Architect ruling quoted in the previous row (accepted behaviour or residue, stated in the PR body); not a follow-up to file. Supersedes the earlier open row, which had labelled it a deferred follow-up.
